question: Explain how a $p\text{-}n$ junction is formed when $p$-type and $n$-type semiconductors are brought into contact. Why is a depletion region produced?

options.A: A p-n junction forms without diffusion or recombination; mobile carriers accumulate at the boundary to form the depletion region.
options.B: Holes diffuse from n-side to p-side and electrons from p-side to n-side, producing a region full of mobile carriers.
options.C: When p-type and n-type semiconductors are joined, holes diffuse p-to-n and electrons n-to-p. They recombine near the junction, leaving fixed acceptor ions on p-side and donor ions on n-side. The carrier-depleted region is the depletion region.
options.D: The depletion region is produced only when a battery is connected; an unbiased junction has no fixed ions.
